title: Hosted GPU depletion corrective program: admission scoring hardening, preemptive scaling, and KV-cache isolation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-25 we observed a hosted API capacity event where GPU pools for region us-west-2 experienced progressive depletion over ~45 minutes. The visible symptom was request latency and a large backlog in the request admission queues followed by degraded throughput and intermittent failures for P1 traffic. This ticket tracks remediation work, verification, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-25 10:13 UTC - Alert: latency SLO breaches triggered for hosted/text-generation endpoints.
2026-02-25 10:18 UTC - Autoscaler attempted ramp; new GPU nodes launched but backpressure continued.
2026-02-25 10:25 UTC - Engineering triage: unusually large batch of low-priority, long-sequence requests observed from several high-throughput customers.
2026-02-25 10:40 UTC - Manual admission gating enabled to throttle new low-priority sessions; KV-cache thrashing observed on several GPUs.
2026-02-25 11:05 UTC - Traffic reroute to secondary pools and temporary quota bumps for critical customers.
2026-02-25 12:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; post-incident diagnostics started.
root_cause: A recent change to the admission scoring heuristic increased the effective weight given to 'batch-friendly' flags without adjusting per-request cost estimates for long-context runs. This caused the admission controller to accept many concurrent requests that looked cheap individually but collectively amplified memory pressure (KV cache churn) and occupancy on GPU instances. The autoscaler reacted but lagged behind the amplification pattern; scale actions were partially ineffective because nodes filled with low-priority work before they could warm up and receive prefetched model state.
action_items:
1) Revert and gate the admission-weight regression: temporarily roll back the admission scoring delta and add a feature-flagged rollout (owner: Ravi Patel) — target 2026-03-03.
2) Implement per-request estimated GPU-cost model used by admission controller (owner: Maria Gonzalez) — design by 2026-03-08, implementation by 2026-03-22.
3) KV-cache isolation: ensure long-context requests use a separate cache partition or eviction policy to avoid thrashing shorter, high-priority sessions (owner: Linh Tran) — prototype by 2026-03-12.
4) Preemptive scale policy: add a predictive autoscale path that reacts to sustained admission rate *and* expected warmup time (owner: Omar Nadeem) — experiment by 2026-03-15.
5) Emergency admission hard limits: add fast-fail thresholds for pools to protect P0 traffic (owner: Ravi Patel) — deploy by 2026-03-05.
6) Add a synthetic workload to chaos tests that reproduces amplification patterns and validate on dedicated test-pools (owner: QA team lead, Priya Singh) — tests added by 2026-03-10.
7) Runbook updates: expand "GPU capacity exhaustion" runbook with step-by-step admission gating, warm pool priming, and rollback checklist (owner: SRE guild) — done 2026-03-04.
progress_updates:
2026-03-01: Reverted admission-weight change in canary; canary pools stable.
2026-03-02: Emergency admission hard limits merged (PR #4521) and rolled to production; immediate reduction in queue amplification observed.
2026-03-03: Runbook updated and published (runbook link below).
2026-03-04: KV-cache isolation design review completed; agreed to prototype per-GPU cache namespaces.
2026-03-05: Per-request cost model specs approved by PM and Research; work scheduled for Cycle 11.
Notes: owners have been assigned and blockers are primarily scheduling and a small infra change to allocator knobs.
review_feedback: Design review (2026-03-04) notes: need clearer SLA-driven priority buckets for admission logic, add telemetry for predicted vs actual cost per request, and ensure any KV-cache isolation respects model sharding. Security reviewed and no data-exfil risk found. PM (Liam O'Connor) suggested adding customer communication templates for quota/behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Admission scoring rollback confirmed and gated behind feature flag.
- Emergency admission limits active and proven to keep P0 endpoints at <1% error during synthetic amplification test.
- KV-cache isolation prototype validated on test pools with <10% perf regression for isolated workloads.
- Predictive autoscale experiment shows 30% faster effective capacity recovery in replayed incident scenario.
- Runbook searchable and linked from on-call pager messages.
notes: Avoided immediate large infra spend by focusing on software controls and smarter admission cost estimation. This ticket coordinates with Dedicated capacity product team to surface longer-term mitigation (reserved CPU-side warming, reserved KV state). We will present a short postmortem to GTM and customer success for affected customers on 2026-03-09.
next_steps:
Finish KV-cache isolation prototype -> run synthetic reproduction -> iterate on per-request cost model -> roll predictive autoscale to staging.
Owner syncs weekly in Capacity Reliability triage (Ravi/Priya/Omar).
